title: The Sky Core Atlas is supreme and any conflicting Agent Artifact provision is invalid to the extent of the conflict
content:
A.1.14.1.1 divides the Sky Atlas's six Scopes into "the first five Scopes [which] define ecosystem-wide rules and governance processes, while the final Scope contains all Agent Artifacts." A.1.14.1.2 names the former group — Governance, Support, Stability, Protocol and Accessibility Scopes plus the Preamble — the **Sky Core Atlas**, holding "the foundational and supreme governance rules, principles, and processes."

A.1.14.1.3 states the precedence rule: all Agent Artifacts "are derived from the Sky Core Atlas and must remain fully consistent with same. Where a provision in an Agent Artifact conflicts with a provision in the Sky Core Atlas, the latter takes precedence and shall supersede the former to the extent of that conflict." A.1.14.1.4 restates it from the other side: "Any Agent Artifact provision that conflicts with the Sky Core Atlas is invalid to the extent of that conflict."

The phrase "to the extent of that conflict" is doing real work — this is severability, not annulment. A conflicting Agent Artifact is not voided wholesale; only the offending provision loses effect, and the rest of the Agent's governance survives. That keeps the supremacy rule usable, because a doctrine that destroyed an entire Artifact over one bad clause would be too costly to invoke and would therefore go unenforced.

The structure is federal rather than unitary: Agents are inside the Atlas, not alongside it, so they inherit its authority and its limits simultaneously. A.1.14.1.7 caps this with a substantive floor that no Artifact text can displace — "No Agent is permitted to take any action that is misaligned with the Spirit of the Atlas."
description: The first five Scopes plus the Preamble form the Sky Core Atlas; the sixth Scope holds all Agent Artifacts, which are derived from it and subordinate to it.
